Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

You are implementing the Convex side of a new "app harness" for Twyne, a writing app at /home/diogenes/Projects/apps/twyne (branch feat/clairic-extraction). Goal: Twyne's model-backed features must be callable through the existing personal-access-token integration API (`POST /api/integrations/v1`, handled in `convex/http.ts`), so the `twyne` CLI, the `twyne-mcp` server and a new eval harness can drive the REAL production code path instead of replaying prompts.

READ FIRST:
1. `convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md` (mandatory Convex rules for this repo).
2. `docs/app-harness.md` — the contract you must implement exactly (operation names, fields, response shapes). Another agent is building the CLI/MCP client against it in parallel, so do not change names or shapes. If something in the contract is genuinely impossible, implement the closest thing, and explain the deviation precisely in your final report.
3. `convex/http.ts` (integration route ~lines 58-280), `convex/integrations.ts` (`authenticate` returns `{ userId }` = the owner's tokenIdentifier, `getFolio`), `convex/agents.ts` (3340 lines: `pickProvider` ~311, `runAdaptiveHostedLlm` ~518, `runLlm` ~738, actions `runInterviewTurn` 1279, `runDossierCheck` 1493, `runPersona` 1643, `suggestRewrite` 1756, `conveneRoom` 1906, `reviewRubric` 2139, `judgeDraft` 2212, `judgeEvidence` 2329, `judgeIntegrity` 2441, `judgeSufficiency` 2618, `judgeTargetFit` 2762, `judgeCustomCriterion` 2872, `judgeRoom` 3120), `convex/lib/personaResearch.ts`, and the rubric panel's hosted path in `src/components/rubric/rubric-panel.tsx` (~lines 330-700) for how a grade is assembled (judgeRoom → sufficiency → evidence/integrity → target fit → `combineJudgesAndStatic` from `src/utils/rubric.ts` → reviewRubric).

THE CORE PROBLEM: every AI action calls `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()` (auth gate, rate-limit identifier, Not Organic DID lookup in `pickProvider` via `identity.subject || identity.tokenIdentifier`, usage capture owner). An httpAction authenticated by a PAT has no Convex identity, so `ctx.runAction(api.agents.x)` would be anonymous. You must refactor so each feature's core logic takes an explicit caller, e.g. `type HostedCaller = { tokenIdentifier: string; subject: string }`:
- Public actions keep their exact args, return values and behaviour: they resolve the caller from `ctx.auth` and call the shared core.
- New internal actions (put them in a new `"use node"` module such as `convex/integrationAi.ts`, or in agents.ts if cleaner) take `caller` (or `ownerId`) explicitly and call the same core.
- `pickProvider` must accept the caller for the Not Organic DID lookup, and `runAdaptiveHostedLlm`'s alias re-pick must thread it through.
- Derive `subject` from the PAT owner's tokenIdentifier (`${issuer}|${subject}`, see `convex/lib/authIdentity.ts`; split at the FIRST `|`).
- Same per-owner rate limits as the browser actions (`consumeRateLimit` keyed by tokenIdentifier).
- `hostedPersonaResearch(ctx)` and the System One review caller rely on ctx.auth today. For the internal path, keep them working as well as you reasonably can without a large refactor. If the editorial review or research is unavailable on the PAT path, say so in your report. Make sure a missing judgement never withholds a note when it would not be withheld in the browser path.

OPERATIONS TO ADD (exact contract in docs/app-harness.md): `editors.list`, `room.convene`, `editor.ask`, `rewrite.suggest`, `rubric.grade`, `dossier.check`, `interview.turn`. Personas come from the built-in cast `src/utils/personas.ts` (`PERSONAS`, ids devil/angel/scholar/editor/reader) mapped to the agent persona shape the actions validate (`personaValidator` in agents.ts: id, name, role, description, focus, plus optional voice fields; drop UI-only fields such as speech voices). `folioId` resolution: when `draftText` is absent and `folioId` is present, load the owner's folio HTML + brief (reuse `internal.integrations.getFolio` or a small internal query) and convert HTML to plain text. `htmlToPlainText` lives in `src/utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`, but that module imports browser code (lix, convex-sync), so move the function into a tiny pure module and re-export it from anti-tabula-rasa so existing callers keep working. For `rubric.grade`, assemble the grade the way the panel's HOSTED path does, and cite the panel lines you mirrored in a comment. Prefer a pure orchestrator module (for example `src/utils/rubric-grade.ts`) that takes judge functions as parameters. Do not refactor the panel itself. Keep http.ts edits localized: one dispatch block delegating to helpers, with field validation that produces 400 errors whose messages pass `integrationPublicError`'s safe-fragment filter (e.g. "draftText is required", "personaId must be one of …").

TESTS: add `convex/integrationAi.test.ts` (convex-test + vitest, following the `import.meta.glob` pattern in `convex/integrations.test.ts`; put `// @vitest-environment node` at the top). Hosted calls in tests go through the legacy OpenAI-compatible route: start a local `node:http` stub server and set `process.env.RIVET_ENDPOINT = "http://127.0.0.1:PORT"` and `RIVET_MODEL`, and make sure `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED` is unset. I verified this works. A probe calling `api.agents.judgeDraft` this way returned `{"provider":"rivet","score":7,...}`, and the stub saw `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the real system prompt. Use `t.fetch("/api/integrations/v1", { method: "POST", headers: { authorization: "Bearer " + token }, body })` with a token from `api.integrations.createToken` called under `t.withIdentity({ tokenIdentifier: "https://twyne.test|w1", subject: "w1", issuer: "https://twyne.test" })`. Cover: each operation's happy path; folioId resolution; a 401 without a token; 400s for missing or invalid fields; that a public action still works unchanged (one regression check is enough). Run ONLY your test file: `npx vitest run convex/integrationAi.test.ts`, plus at most one targeted existing test such as `npx vitest run convex/integrations.test.ts`. Do NOT run the full test suite (it takes over 10 minutes), and run `tsc` at most once at the end, scoped to what you touched if possible.

CODEGEN: `convex/_generated/api.d.ts` must list any new module. Try `npx convex codegen`. If it fails or wants to push or deploy, hand-edit api.d.ts following its existing pattern instead. NEVER run `convex deploy`, `convex dev`, or anything that pushes to a deployment.

SHARED CHECKOUT RULES (important): two other agent threads are editing this same working tree right now (Typst work and a share-button fix), and there are ~100 uncommitted files from earlier work. Do NOT run git commands that change state (no stash, checkout, reset, restore, commit, add). Do not revert or reformat files you did not need to touch. Re-read a file immediately before editing it. Do not run prettier or eslint --fix over the repo. `convex/agents.ts` already has a small uncommitted diff, so preserve it. Do not touch `packages/twyne-tools/` (another agent owns it) or `evals/app/` (I own it).

Match the surrounding code style (comment density, naming, the existing prose-y doc comments). Final report: list every file you changed or added; describe the caller refactor; note any contract deviations, test results (pasted summary lines), and known gaps (research and System One review on the PAT path, rate-limit implications for batch evals).

# App harness: AI operations over the integration API, CLI and MCP

Twyne's model-backed features (the room of editors, rewrites, the rubric, the
dossier check and the dossier interview) are reachable from outside the
browser through the same authenticated boundary the folio tools already use:
`POST /api/integrations/v1` with a personal access token. The `twyne` CLI and
the `twyne-mcp` server in `packages/twyne-tools` expose them, and the app evals
in `evals/app/` drive them through MCP, so an eval exercises the production
path rather than a replay of its prompts.

```
eval runner ──MCP──▶ twyne-mcp tools ──TwyneClient──▶ /api/integrations/v1
                                                       │  (PAT → owner)
                                                       ▼
                                 internal actions in convex/ (same code the
                                 browser's api.agents.* actions run)
                                                       │
                                                       ▼
                                 hosted provider: Not Organic, or the legacy
                                 OpenAI-compatible route (RIVET_ENDPOINT)
```

## Operations

Every request is `{ "operation": "<name>", ...fields }` and every success is
`{ "ok": true, "data": ... }`, exactly like the folio operations. Failures are
`{ "ok": false, "error": "..." }` with the same public-error filtering.

Shared field types:

- `draftText: string` — the manuscript as plain text.
- `folioId: string` — alternative to `draftText`. The server loads the
  owner's folio, converts its HTML to plain text, and uses the folio's brief
  when `brief` is not supplied. Supplying neither is a 400.
- `brief: ProjectBrief | null` — the dossier (`convex/agents.ts`
  `projectBriefValidator`). Optional everywhere except `dossier.check`.
- `responseLocale: "en" | "fr" | "es" | "zh" | "hi" | "ja"` — optional.
- `writerProfile` — optional, `writerProfileValidator` shape.
- `personaId` — one of the built-in editors in `src/utils/personas.ts`:
  `devil`, `angel`, `scholar`, `editor`, `reader`.

`EditorNote`:

```ts
{
  personaId: string;
  personaName: string;
  text: string;
  type: "critique" | "suggestion" | "encouragement" | "perspective";
  provider: string;          // "local" means the hosted model was not used
  anchor?: string;           // verbatim passage pinned by quote_passage
  anchors?: string[];
  extractions?: unknown[];
  traceId?: string;
}
```

| operation         | fields                                                                                                                                 | `data`                              |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `editors.list`    | —                                                                                                                                      | `Array<{ id, name, role, description, focus }>` |
| `room.convene`    | `draftText`\|`folioId`, `brief?`, `personaIds?` (default: all five), `writerProfile?`, `responseLocale?`, `newMaterial?`, `trajectory?` | `{ notes: EditorNote[] }`           |
| `editor.ask`      | `personaId`, `draftText`\|`folioId`, `brief?`, `instruction?` (`feedback`\|`elaborate`\|`riff`\|`rewrite-suggestion`), `userMessage?`, `priorMessages?`, `anchor?`, `writerProfile?`, `responseLocale?` | `{ note: EditorNote }` |
| `rewrite.suggest` | `personaId`, `draftText`\|`folioId`, `original`, `level` (`sentence`\|`paragraph`), `brief?`, `writerProfile?`, `responseLocale?`         | `{ replacement, rationale, provider }` |
| `rubric.grade`    | `draftText`\|`folioId`, `brief?`, `criteria?: Array<{ label, description }>`, `responseLocale?`                                            | `RubricGrade` (below)               |
| `dossier.check`   | `brief`, `draftText`\|`folioId`, `responseLocale?`                                                                                      | `{ observations, provider }`        |
| `interview.turn`  | `messages: Array<{ author: "writer"\|"interviewer", text }>`, `mode` (`first-run`\|`refine`), `currentBrief?`, `startingMaterial?`, `responseLocale?` | `InterviewTurnResult` (as `runInterviewTurn` returns) |

`RubricGrade` mirrors what the rubric panel computes on its hosted path:

```ts
{
  grade: string;            // letter grade from combineJudgesAndStatic
  combined: number;
  judgeMean: number;
  minJudge: number;
  staticTotal: number;
  staticFeedback: string[];
  judges: Array<{ personaId: string; score: number; rationale: string; provider: string }>;
  sufficiency: { score: number; rationale: string; provider: string };
  evidence: { score: number; rationale: string; provider: string };
  integrity: { score: number; rationale: string; provider: string };
  targetFit: { score: number; rationale: string; provider: string };
  custom: Array<{ label: string; score: number; rationale: string; provider: string }>;
  review: { text: string; provider: string } | null;
}
```

Model-backed operations apply the same per-owner rate limits as the browser
actions. Results are returned, not written to the folio.

## Running the app locally for tests and evals

`evals/app/local-app.ts` loads every module in `convex/` into one process with
`convex-test`, seeds a writer and an access token, and serves the real HTTP
router. Hosted calls go wherever the environment points them:

- `--model mock` starts a scripted OpenAI-compatible stub and sets
  `RIVET_ENDPOINT` to it, so the legacy hosted route answers from fixtures.
- `--model openai-compatible` uses `TWYNE_APP_MODEL_BASE_URL`,
  `TWYNE_APP_MODEL_API_KEY` and `TWYNE_APP_MODEL` through the same route.
- `--model notorganic` keeps the app's Not Organic routing and links the
  seeded writer to `TWYNE_EVAL_DID`.

```sh
bun evals/app/local-app.ts --model mock --port 8788
# prints TWYNE_API_URL and TWYNE_ACCESS_TOKEN for the CLI and twyne-mcp
```

The Convex side of the app harness is implemented, typechecks, and its tests pass. Nothing else is pending, so here is the report.

## Files

Added:
- `convex/integrationAi.ts` ("use node"): internal actions `conveneRoom`, `askEditor`, `suggestRewrite`, `gradeRubric`, `checkDossier`, `interviewTurn`, each taking `ownerId` and calling the shared cores.

- `src/utils/html-to-plain-text.ts`: the dependency-free converter.
- `convex/integrationAi.test.ts`: 13 tests.

Modified:
- `convex/agents.ts`: the caller refactor (below), plus `judgeRoom`'s hosted results now carry `provider: provider.label` like the local ones already did. The panel's `JudgeResult` type already declared that field.
- `convex/http.ts`: one `default:` branch delegating AI operations, "Too many requests" added to the safe fragments with a 429 status, and structured application errors (`ConvexError` data with `code` and `message`) passed through as `{ ok: false, error, code }` with a matching status.
- `convex/lib/authIdentity.ts`: `subjectFromTokenIdentifier` (splits at the first `|`).
- `src/utils/anti-tabula-rasa.ts`: imports and re-exports `htmlToPlainText`.
- `convex/_generated/api.d.ts`: regenerated by `npx convex codegen` (no push). It also picked up another agent's untracked `preferences.ts` and `preferenceValidators.ts`, which is correct for the working tree.

## Caller refactor

`HostedCaller = { tokenIdentifier, subject }` is now threaded through `pickProvider` (Not Organic link lookup uses `caller.subject`), `runAdaptiveHostedLlm` including its alias re-pick, `runLlm`, and `runHostedAgent`. Twelve actions were split into a thin public wrapper that resolves the caller from `ctx.auth` and a `*Core(ctx, caller, args)` function; `analyzeRoom`, `judgeDraft` and `suggestRubricCriteria` resolve a `caller` inline. Args validators were hoisted to `<name>Args` constants so the cores are typed with `ObjectType`. Public args, return values and the rate limits inside the bodies are unchanged. The uncommitted Portkey removal was preserved. The diff is large because the extracted bodies dropped one indentation level.

- Failure bodies may carry an extra `code` field when the core threw an application error.

## Known gaps

- `hostedPersonaResearch` and the System One review call public actions gated on `ctx.auth`, so on the PAT path editors write without extraction tools and notes are released unreviewed. A missing judgement never withholds a note, same as the browser path.
- Rate limits are the browser ones per owner: room convene 6/min, feedback and rewrites 30/min. A batch eval convening the room repeatedly will hit 429s and should pace itself or use several tokens' owners.

The gap is closed. The token path now runs the same research tools and the same System One review gate as the browser, through one shared implementation.

## Files

Added:
- `convex/lib/hostedTransports.ts`: `judgementTransport()` and `extractionTransport()` plus `directExtractionCredentials()`, the environment-only precedence rules both action modules and the research wiring now share.

Modified:
- `convex/systemOne.ts`: `ask` is a thin wrapper over `askCore(ctx, caller | null, args)`. New `askAs` internal action takes `ownerId`. Same transports, same `userIsPro` check and `systemOne:ask` rate limit keyed by the caller's tokenIdentifier, Not Organic link looked up by `caller.subject`. `TYPESAFE_BASE_URL` overrides the direct endpoint only when set.
- `convex/extraction.ts`: same split into `extract`, `extractCore` and the internal `extractAs`. The in-flight Clairic changes (validated body, model regex, error mapping) are intact.
- `convex/lib/personaResearch.ts`: `hostedPersonaResearch(ctx, caller)` reads availability from the transport helpers, looks up the link with `internal.providerIdentity.getLinkedDidBySubject` by `caller.subject`, and binds `extract` and `judge` to `extractAs` and `askAs` with the caller's owner id.
- `convex/agents.ts`: the System One reviewer in `runAdaptiveHostedLlm` calls `internal.systemOne.askAs` with the caller; both research call sites pass the caller. `HostedCaller`, `callerFromIdentity` and `callerFromTokenIdentifier` moved to `convex/lib/authIdentity.ts` so the three modules share them, with a re-export from agents.ts for `integrationAi.ts`.
- `convex/integrationAi.ts`: header comment updated, no behaviour change.
- `convex/integrationAi.test.ts`: the stub now also answers `/v1/systemone` and records offered tools. Five new tests.
- `src/utils/persona-research.test.ts`: the server transport test passes a caller and expects the `*As` actions.
- `convex/_generated/api.d.ts`: regenerated by codegen.

## Tests

```
convex/integrationAi.test.ts      Tests  18 passed (18)
convex/integrations.test.ts       Tests  3 passed (3)
src/utils/persona-research.test.ts  11 pass, 0 fail   (bun)
convex/extraction.test.ts           45 pass, 0 fail   (bun)
```
The integrations run again lists a stale `.stryker-tmp` sandbox copy as a failed file. It is not the real test. Convex `tsc` is clean apart from the pre-existing `extraction.test.ts` error.

New coverage on the PAT path:
- `editor.ask` with a draft the stub reviewer scores "Useless" on `helpful` drafts twice. The second prompt carries the private revision directions naming `helpful`, the reviewer sees both candidates with the note-gate and policy questions, and the released note is the revision.
- A note the reviewer accepts is drafted once and judged once.
- With direct extraction credentials, the model is offered `quote_passage`, `find_passages`, `extract` and `judge`. Without them, `quote_passage` and `judge` only.
- Public `systemOne.ask` still returns `{ ok: false, error: "signed out" }` to an anonymous caller without reaching the stub.

## What still differs between browser and token paths

- Nothing in the editorial pipeline. Provider pick, research tools, review gate, redraft loop, rate limits and usage capture all run from one core with the caller supplied either way.
- The browser's BYOK layer sits above this: a writer with their own provider or TypeSafe key in Settings gets client-side judges and `apiKey` relays that the token path never uses. The token path is always the hosted path.
- Note streaming to the panel is browser-only. The token path returns the finished note.
- `userIsPro` is consulted on both paths for the System One and extraction tiers, so a token owner without a Not Organic link gets the free-tier limits, as a signed-in free account does.
